component: P16 inbox accounting and supervised concurrency assurance
constraints: Local opaque immutable payloads: at most sixteen items, one MiB summed payload bytes, a per-peer quota and at most sixty seconds caller-time retention.
One lock protects purge, accounting, admission and removal. Invalid or regressing caller time clears and closes; rejection preserves live queued entries.
Assurance must exercise the actual Python queue with two producers while preventing a deadlocked test worker from trapping the test runner.
alternatives: CPython deque plus lock with explicit compound quota and lifetime checks; subprocess supervision of the existing Python concurrency probe.
Rust crossbeam bounded channels plus explicit byte, peer and arbitrary-expiry accounting.
C#/F# System.Threading.Channels bounded channels with explicit compound quota/lifetime accounting.
Erlang/Elixir processes with explicitly bounded mailbox admission and quota accounting.
rationale: KEEP the explicit atomic accounting boundary for this small synchronous queue: item count, summed bytes, peer quota and expiry behind a live head require a single consistent decision. A count-bounded channel alone does not provide these semantics.

BEAM isolation is relevant to service fault containment but ordinary message queues do not supply this compound admission contract. Native and managed channel alternatives still need the contract-specific accounting layer.

Fix assurance within Python: executor context shutdown waits for workers after a future timeout. A child process runs the real queue probe; subprocess.run kills and waits for that direct child on timeout.

A controlled lock-acquisition fault trapped the former test past its future timeout. The same injected fault now returns an assertion failure within the outer supervisor window; the normal two-producer case and dedicated timeout regression pass.
No target deadline or memory envelope supports a runtime migration or performance ranking. This decision does not rely on installation, familiarity or rewrite cost.
limits: Payload-byte limits are not heap/RSS bounds; lock wait, fairness and idle expiry are not bounded by this API. Previously returned bytes remain reachable after close.
Subprocess supervision is test-only, not a runtime watchdog or sandbox. Process creation can delay timeout delivery; no exact hard wall-clock bound is claimed.
The trusted child has two threads, no descendant processes and fixed small output. This helper is not safe execution of arbitrary scripts or an output-quota mechanism.
One sampled two-producer schedule does not exhaust interleavings or prove scheduler fairness. No hardware latency, resource qualification or whole-lane completion.
